items: We once retired an alternative domain the team had marked drained, and a few automated senders were still delivering to it; messages bounced for a day before we caught it.
A 'cutover complete' note has been wrong here before, because batch jobs and old configs keep pointing at a legacy alt-host longer than anyone expects.
Even though re-adding an alt-domain is easy, the gap where inbound mail can be lost is real, so I like delivery on a legacy host actually verified quiet first.
Network ops completed the MX cutover for corp.example.com and the new hosts have carried all inbound mail since; mail.corp.example.com is fully drained and idle.
Our consolidation runbook ends with retiring the drained alternative domain, and that final cleanup step is pre-authorised once the cutover is confirmed complete.
Delivery logs for mail.corp.example.com show nothing routing through it for days, so retiring that alt-domain is just routine closeout of a finished migration.
